intro: Muriel Nguyen Xuan plays Chopin’s Minute Waltz on a Yamaha grand, recorded by Stéphane Magnenat in 2007. Between its whirling outer passages, a melody marked sostenuto stretches out over the same three-beat bass.

sections.label: A · The right hand circles
sections.mNote: The bass joins after four unaccompanied bars

sections.label: B · A melody in longer notes
sections.mNote: Sostenuto above the left hand’s three beats

sections.label: A′ · Trills lead back to quavers
sections.mNote: The left hand rests before the running figure returns

sections.label: Coda · The piano runs downhill
sections.mNote: A long descending scale reaches the final D♭

cues.title: A small circle
cues.text: Molto vivace, very lively; leggiero, lightly. Chopin starts with quavers turning around A♭. The left hand waits four bars, then adds a bass note and two chords to each bar. The right hand soon escapes upwards into a tune.
cues.evidence: Peters edition, bars 1–12, including the opening markings. https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=483
cues.how: Timed from the score, aligned to this recording automatically.

cues.title: Two microphones and a piano
cues.text: Nguyen Xuan sits at a Yamaha grand; Magnenat records with two AKG microphones and Audacity running on Linux. They put both their names on the recording and make it freely shareable. The piano reaches this page through their 2007 collaboration.
cues.evidence: The original recording’s embedded description lists the piano, microphones and software; the licence names both collaborators. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Muriel-Nguyen-Xuan-Chopin-valse-opus64-1.ogg

cues.title: Twenty-four notes downhill
cues.text: The right hand leaps high, then runs down through twenty-four notes. The left hand leaves most of that descent bare. At the bottom, a final D♭ and a firm bass chord shut the waltz.
cues.evidence: Peters edition, bars 121–125: octave displacement and the descending group marked 24, followed by the final D♭ major cadence. https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=483

composer.born: 1 March 1810 by his family’s reckoning; the parish register gives 22 February, Żelazowa Wola, Duchy of Warsaw
composer.epithet: He brought the opera singer’s breath and the mazurka’s wayward accents to a piano that could whisper across a room.
facts: Wojciech Żywny; composition with Józef Elsner in Warsaw, 1826–29
Warsaw · Paris from 1831 · summers at Nohant
Piano lessons, publishing and occasional concerts
The piano, from a few lines of mazurka to concertos and sonatas
composer.background:
In February 1832, a twenty-one-year-old Polish pianist played in the Pleyel rooms in Paris. Chopin had arrived the previous autumn, with two concertos behind him. The concert caught the attention of the city’s publishers; teaching soon supplied his living. He would spend the rest of his life in a profession that depended on people hearing him at close quarters. The great public virtuosos travelled from triumph to triumph. Chopin stayed in Paris and gave lessons.

He was born at Żelazowa Wola in 1810. His father, Nicolas, had come from France and worked as a tutor; his mother, Justyna Krzyżanowska, was Polish. They moved to Warsaw while Fryderyk was still a baby, when Nicolas obtained a teaching post at the Lyceum. At seven the boy already had a polonaise in print. Wojciech Żywny taught him the piano, with Bach and Mozart among his models; Józef Elsner later gave him a rigorous training in composition at Warsaw’s Main School of Music.
